smeGate.notes: AI technical pre-review (2026-08, see technicalPreReview below) returned 5 PASS / 9 REWORD / 1 RETUNE / 0 REMOVE. The one learner-exposure-blocking item — hierarchy-independent-walks — has been substantively retuned in code (true conditional hierarchical walk; L2 sees only L1 demand misses). The nine reword dispositions have been applied to rule claims/realWorldBasis. REVIEW SCOPE INSTRUCTION: judge each rule by ONE question — 'if a learner sees this causal relationship repeatedly, does it teach a safe real-world diagnostic heuristic?' Do NOT review numerical realism unless the number itself affects the learner's decision rule (e.g. whether 120 cycles is realistic is out of scope; whether repeated exposure teaches 'all misses cost roughly the same' is in scope). Domain remains LOCKED for learner exposure until a HUMAN reviewer sets smeGate.reviewer/reviewedAt and verdict SIGNED_OFF. An AI must never write its own name into smeGate. Once signed, treat that domainVersion as immutable: any later causal-rule or threshold change must invalidate sign-off and bump the domain version.

technicalPreReview.summary: Rules most likely to train bad habits are not the declared fictions but the plausible compressed heuristics (spread-misses=>capacity, first-touch=>measured-miss, useful-prefetch=>faster, fewer-misses=>proportionally-faster, 80% same-word=>true sharing). All such heuristics are now labelled as generated-world separators, not hardware laws. hierarchy-independent-walks was the sole causal blocker and has been retuned in code.
technicalPreReview.authority: PREPARES evidence only; cannot certify teaching physics as human-reviewed.

rules.title: Set index = (line address) mod setCount
rules.claim: Consecutive cache lines map to consecutive sets; addresses L apart share a set iff their line indices are congruent mod setCount.
rules.realWorldBasis: Standard bit-sliced set selection for non-hashed caches; matches textbook set-associative indexing.

rules.title: LRU replacement: hit refreshes recency; eviction removes least-recent line
rules.claim: A hit moves the line to MRU position; a miss into a full set evicts the LRU line. Eviction count increments only on capacity pressure.
rules.realWorldBasis: Canonical LRU. Real hardware approximates LRU (pseudo-LRU, adaptive policies); tie-breaking and PLRU differences affect exact miss counts, not directionality.

rules.title: More hot lines than associativity in one set => cyclic thrash
rules.claim: When a cyclic access pattern touches > associativity distinct lines of a single set, every iteration misses because each pass evicts lines later passes need. Set skew becomes extreme; total footprint stays tiny.
rules.realWorldBasis: Textbook conflict-miss mechanism; directionally certain. Exact skew magnitudes are recipe artifacts, not hardware claims.

rules.title: Working set exceeding cache => misses spread across sets with reuse present
rules.claim: Sweeping data larger than the cache yields misses distributed across many sets; lines have reuse but are evicted before reuse distance closes. MODEL SEPARATOR, not a hardware law: in these generated worlds a spread pattern with low reuse points at the capacity family. Real capacity pressure can also look concentrated (poorly distributed hash) and real spatial-locality loss also spreads — the discriminator is safe only inside this model.
rules.realWorldBasis: Definitional for capacity misses that the working set exceeding the cache causes eviction-before-reuse; but 'evenly spread' is a property of these recipes' uniform sweeps, and real caches with hashed indexing distribute differently.
rules.diagnosticHeuristicTrained: spread misses + low reuse => working-set/capacity family (MODEL-ONLY separator; verify against footprint size before trusting on real hardware)

smeReview.reviewerNote: AI pre-review: REWORD applied — spread-pattern heuristic labelled a generated-world separator.

rules.title: First touch of a line is conceptually a cold miss, though hardware prefetch can hide it from demand-miss counters
rules.kernel: sim.ts SetAssocLru (any miss to unseen tag)
rules.claim: Fresh-data walks produce near-100% first-touch DEMAND miss rates in this model. DISTINCTION REQUIRED: a conceptual compulsory (cold) miss always happens on first touch; whether it shows up in an observed demand-miss counter depends on hardware prefetch having already fetched the line. Our model accounts for prefetch through the separate prefetch channel — so a learner comparing these readings to real machines must expect real first-touch misses to be partially hidden.
rules.realWorldBasis: The cold/compulsory category is textbook-standard. The deviation is in OBSERVATION: real counters under next-line prefetchers often show far fewer apparent cold misses than the conceptual count.

smeReview.reviewerNote: AI pre-review: REWORD applied — conceptual vs observed cold-miss distinction added.

rules.title: Scattered/strided access uses most of each line once => miss rate approaches the compulsory floor WHEN the stream is fresh and reuse-free
rules.kernel: construct.ts (gather-scatter, column-walk recipes); analyze.ts gapPattern classification
rules.claim: CONDITIONAL MECHANISM: when a scattered/wide-stride pattern touches few bytes per line AND the stream is large/fresh enough that lines are not re-referenced before eviction, nearly every access misses. It is NOT true of every strided workload: short strides over small resident arrays hit heavily. The gap-pattern bins (contiguous <=1.2 lines, short-stride <=4, long-stride <=40, else scatter) are arbitrary boundaries chosen for SOLVER SEPARABILITY in generated worlds — they are not perceptual or hardware boundaries, and no real diagnostic meaning attaches to 1.3 vs 1.1 mean-gap.
rules.realWorldBasis: Directionally standard (poor spatial locality raises miss rate) with explicit preconditions. Real strided workloads can hit well when multiple elements per line are used or arrays fit in cache.
rules.diagnosticHeuristicTrained: scatter/long-stride gaps + once-used lines => spatial-locality family (valid only for fresh, larger-than-cache streams)

smeReview.reviewerNote: AI pre-review: REWORD applied — freshness/size conditions added; bins labelled solver-separability boundaries.

rules.title: Reuse exists but reuse distance exceeds cache => temporal locality loss
rules.claim: Interleaving two large streams preserves per-line reuse but inflates reuse distance past cache size, so lines evict before re-use. Signature: spread misses with reuse factor >1 but ineffective.
rules.realWorldBasis: Standard reuse-distance reasoning. Simplification: single flat cache instead of stack-distance profile.

rules.title: Degree-1 next-line prefetch: one issue per demand miss; model-useful iff L+1 demanded later
rules.claim: In THIS MODEL, prefetch usefulness equals the fraction of issued lines whose successor line appears anywhere later in the demand stream. Sequential sweeps approach ~100% useful; scattered streams approach 0%. The diagnostic thresholds ('healthy >=50%', 'defeated <35%') are MODEL-RELATIVE SEPARATORS for generated worlds, not hardware measurements — real prefetcher behaviour has no such universal boundaries.
rules.realWorldBasis: Real next-line prefetchers behave this way directionally. REAL DEVIATIONS, all unmodelled: (1) TIMELINESS — a real prefetch only helps if it arrives before the demand; ours counts L+1 as useful regardless of order; (2) ADAPTATION — real prefetchers train, boost degrees, and throttle; ours never adapts; (3) POLLUTION — useless prefetched lines evict useful ones in real caches; our cache does not track prefetch fills. Net effect: our useful-fraction OVERSTATES real-world effectiveness on mixed streams.
rules.diagnosticHeuristicTrained: prefetch audit fraction separates storm/starved from healthy streaming INSIDE this model's threshold conventions

smeReview.reviewerNote: AI pre-review: REWORD applied — timeliness/adaptation/pollution named as unmodelled; thresholds labelled model-relative.

rules.title: Useful prefetches shorten effective miss penalty by min(0.8, 0.9 x usefulFraction)
rules.claim: Cycle estimate multiplies the flat miss penalty by (1 - hideFactor); useless prefetches add 2 cycles each on top.
rules.realWorldBasis: FICTIONAL COUPLING CONSTANT: real penalty reduction depends on memory-level parallelism, timing overlap, and queue occupancy — none modeled. The 0.9/0.8 numbers encode 'mostly helpful, capped' intuition only. Direction is CONDITIONAL in reality: bandwidth saturation, cache pollution from useless prefetches, and queue pressure can make MORE prefetching slower, a relationship this model cannot express. Never quote cycle counts as physical; never teach 'useful prefetch always helps'.
rules.diagnosticHeuristicTrained: within this model, more useful prefetching => faster; the REVERSE (prefetching hurts) occurs on real hardware under bandwidth/pollution pressure and is out of model scope

smeReview.reviewerNote: AI pre-review: REWORD applied — heuristic made conditional; reversal conditions named.

rules.title: Every miss costs 120 cycles; coherence transfer costs 90 cycles
rules.claim: Additive stall accounting: baseCpi x accesses + hits x 0 + misses x 120 + transfers x 90 (+ prefetch bus cost).
rules.realWorldBasis: FICTIONAL CONSTANTS: real penalties vary by level hit in (L2/L3/DRAM), row-buffer state, contention, and overlap (MLP) — see Intel Optimization Reference Manual's treatment of multi-level memory behaviour. Flat constants preserve ordering between worlds but absolute cycle numbers are meaningless. The trained heuristic is deliberately restricted: slowdown RATIOS within one world's baseline comparison are directionally defensible; 'fewer misses => proportionally faster' across different workloads is NOT a safe real-world inference because different misses have wildly different costs and overlap.
rules.diagnosticHeuristicTrained: within a single world, miss-driven slowdown dominates; ratio reasoning vs the baseline only — never cross-workload proportionality

smeReview.reviewerNote: AI pre-review: REWORD applied — proportionality claim restricted to within-world ratio reasoning.

rules.title: Writer alternation on shared lines produces cross-core invalidations; no protocol states
rules.claim: Each write to a line last written by the other core counts as one cross-core invalidation; contended-line count and local writes tracked alongside. Same-word conflicts counted independently at word granularity.
rules.realWorldBasis: Ledger abstraction over MESI-family protocols. Directionally sound: alternating writers on a shared line DO force ownership transfers, and line-granular contention is exactly the class Linux perf c2c is designed to expose. IMPORTANT CALIBRATION: this synthetic ledger is an ATTRIBUTION abstraction, not literal hardware protocol evidence — real c2c/HITM analysis is cache-line oriented and protocol-aware (MESI states, directory vs snoop), whereas our word-level tracking is a diagnostic device. MISSING entirely: upgrade/invalidate distinctions, write-broadcast policies, DMA/peripheral-induced invalidation. Same-word tracking is what makes true/false sharing separable in generated worlds.
rules.diagnosticHeuristicTrained: cross-core traffic present + high same-word share => true sharing; low share => false sharing (attribution heuristic within the model, to be confirmed by line-level tooling on real systems)

smeReview.reviewerNote: AI pre-review: REWORD applied — HITM 'mirrors' softened to attribution analogy; c2c is line-oriented.

rules.title: Same-word conflicts > 80% of cross-core invalidations => classify as TRUE sharing
rules.claim: True sharing (both cores writing the SAME word) shows mostly same-word conflicts; false sharing (different words, one line) shows mostly different-word conflicts. The 80% boundary is a GENERATED-WORLD SEPARATOR chosen so worlds are solvable — there is NO universal 80% threshold on real hardware, and real workloads routinely mix both modes on one line.
rules.realWorldBasis: Directionally defensible attribution heuristic mirroring HITM-style analysis. CAVEAT: real traces are messy — mixed-mode lines, multiple sharers, and sampling artifacts mean real analysis looks at distributions across lines, not a single-line binary. Learners should treat the clean 0/80/100 splits seen here as lab conditions that rarely occur in production profiles.
rules.diagnosticHeuristicTrained: same-word share decides which sharing pathology — VALID ONLY for clean-mode cases; expect mixed evidence in real profiles

smeReview.reviewerNote: AI pre-review: REWORD applied — 80% labelled purely a generated-world separator.

rules.title: Two-level hierarchy: TRUE conditional walk — L2 sees only L1's demand misses
rules.claim: The stream enters L1; only L1 demand misses are presented to L2, so L2's access count and miss rate are CONDITIONAL on L1 behaviour, as in a real inclusive hierarchy. (Pre-review retune, implemented 2026-08: replaces the earlier independent same-stream runs that presented counterfactual cache sizes as hierarchy levels.)
rules.realWorldBasis: Causally correct traffic direction: lower levels see higher-level misses. DISCLOSED RESIDUAL SIMPLIFICATION: a real inclusive hierarchy also forwards EVICTED lines downward (back-invalidation) and applies inclusion policy; this walk forwards demand misses only, so L2 miss counts can understate inclusive-design reality. Absolute per-level rates are model quantities; the QUALITATIVE reading (misses migrate to the level whose size the working set approaches) is the defensible part.
rules.diagnosticHeuristicTrained: working set near/above a level's size => misses migrate to that level

smeReview.reviewerNote: AI pre-review: RETUNE — was the sole causal blocker; substantive code retune implemented and verified (conditional L2 accesses = L1 miss count). Human confirmation still required.

rules.title: Slowdown measured against a known-good twin workload — a LAB CONSTRUCT, not a production baseline
rules.claim: Each world embeds a healthy variant of the same workload shape; slowdown = regressed cycles / benign cycles. Baseline miss rate typically 3–7%.
rules.realWorldBasis: Methodological simplification presented as fact: real regression triage compares against historical profiles of THE SAME binary, which drift (data changes, load changes, co-tenancy) and are rarely clean twins. The compare-before-concluding lesson transfers; the existence of a pristine reference does not. Learner-facing material must label the twin as a lab construct.
rules.diagnosticHeuristicTrained: compare current against a known-good reference before concluding regression (reference quality varies in production — the clean twin here is a lab convenience)

smeReview.reviewerNote: AI pre-review: REWORD applied — twin explicitly labelled lab construct.

rules.title: Timeline windows share cache state; cold-start pollution affects early windows only
rules.claim: Eight sequential windows over one continuous stream; window boundaries do not reset cache state. Phase labels attach windows to workload phases when multiple phases exist.
rules.realWorldBasis: Correct for continuous profiling. Window SIZE (stream/8) is arbitrary; real profilers use time slices. Phase-window alignment in phase-change worlds assumes phases align to stream fractions — a recipe property, slightly idealized vs real phase detection.

notModeled: TLB / page-table walk effects (explicitly omitted rather than fake-countered)
store buffering / memory disambiguation / OoO MLP overlap
bus contention feedback between concurrent misses and prefetches
MESI protocol state machine (ledger abstraction instead)
cache hashing (slice/hash-indexed real caches defeat simple bit-slicing)
sampling noise in counters (field scaffolded, deliberately disabled)
